§ 3VEDIC AGE

Vedic Age (1500-600 BC)

  • Early Vedic Age (1500-1000 BC) → They were pastoral community
  • Later Vedic Age (1000-600 BC)
  • Bogazkoi inscription (Turkey): It mentioned names such as Indra, Varun, etc.

Note:

  • It is believed that Aryans arrived from Central Asia, where one group migrated from Turkey towards Europe and other came towards India.
  • Language of Aryans: Sanskrit
  • Aryans are considered to have codified the Vedas.

Similar sounding words

WordMeaning
BrahtaBrother
SaptaSeven
AndarUnder

VEDAS

  • There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda.
  • Oldest Text: Compiled during Zend-Avesta (Iran).
  • Meaning: Knowledge.
  • They were orally passed (Shruti) from one generation to another.
  • Apaurusheya: It is not created by man but gifted by God.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak

  • He compiled the book: The Arctic Home in the Vedas (he said "all Indians were Aryans").

Subdivisions of Vedas

SamhitaBrahmanasAranyakasUpanishads
Collection of Hymns (Sukta)Sacrifices and RitualsHermits (those who lived in jungles)Bhakti (talks about Bhakti Marga)

Rig Veda

  • It was the first Veda to be compiled.
  • It is made up of 10 mandalas.
  • It has the oldest and largest collection of Sanskrit hymns.
  • Total: 1028 hymns
  • Verses: 10,600
  • Hymns recited by Hotri.
  • Deities: Indra, Agni, Vishnu, and Varuna.
  • Female deities: Aditi, Usha (goddess of dawn).
  • Gayatri Mantra was written by Sage Vishwamitra for Goddess Savitri (mentioned in 3rd mandala).
  • Mandala no. 2-7 were created first.
  • 10th mandala mentions Purusha Sukta (considered a cosmic being).

Note: Upanishads are also known as "Vedanta" (end of Vedas).

Total: 108 Upanishads (Traditional)

Purusha Sukta

  • Mouth: Brahmans
  • Arms: Kshatriya
  • Thighs: Vaishya
  • Feet: Shudra

These four varnas are believed to have emerged from different parts of Purusha.

  • 9th mandala mentions: Lord Soma (Lord of Plants).
  • Somras is an energy drink.

Sama Veda

  • It is the oldest book on music.
  • It consists of chanting melodies.
  • It is composed of two Upanishads → Chandogya and Kena

Yajur Veda

  • It is the collection of mantras (rituals and sacrifices).
  • It is divided into two section → Shukla (meaning: White; contains Sathapatha Brahmana) and Krishna (meaning: Black).

Jabala Upanishad is a part of Yajur Veda.

Important Upanishads

  • Brihadaranyaka (oldest Upanishad).
  • Katha (contains story of Nachiketa and Yama (God of Death)).

Atharva Veda

  • Veda of magic formulas to ward off evil spirits and diseases (black magic).
  • It is divided into 20 khandas.

Important Upanishads of Atharva Veda

  • Mundaka Upanishad: Satyameva Jayate taken from here.
  • Maha Upanishad: Vasudhaiva Kutumbhkam (meaning: "the whole world is one family") taken from Chapter 6 of Maha Upanishad.
  • Mandukya Upanishad.

6 Schools of Philosophy

SchoolPropounded By
Samkhya (oldest of all)Kapila
NyayaGautam (scientific approach)
VaisheshikaKanada (metaphysics) → Kanada proposed that all substances are composed of indivisible particles called "Parmanu" (atoms).
YogaPatanjali
Uttar Mimansa (Vedanta)Badrayana
Purva MimansaJaimini

Vedangas

  • They are tools to understand Vedas.
  • They are philosophical teachings of Upanishads.
  • There are total six Vedangas.
VedangaStudy of
SikshaStudy of phonetics
KalpaStudy of practices
VyankaranStudy of grammar
NiruktaStudy of etymology
JyotiStudy of light
ChhandaStudy of poetic matters

Early Vedic Age: Rig Veda

  • Mention of Himvanta (Himalaya) and Munjavat (Hindu Kush) in Rig Veda.
  • Mention of Sapta Sindhu in Rig Veda.

§ 4VEDIC AGE

Battle of 10 Kings

  • Battle of 10 Kings (Dasarajna Yuddha) mentioned in the 7th mandala of Rig Veda.
  • Between: Bharata tribe (leader: Sudas) vs 10 kings.
  • Won by: Bharata tribe
  • It was fought on the banks of Purushini (Ravi river).

Society

  • The society was divided into four varnas.
  • Varna system was not hereditary, but based on profession.
  • Child marriage was not prevalent.
TermMeaning
Widow RemarriageNiyogya (was allowed)
SocietyThe condition of women was good
Cow (Aghanya meaning sacred)Cow was considered as wealth decider (Gomat: wealthy person)
GavishthiBattle for Cows

Polity

  • Elective monarchy.
BodyFunction
SabhaCommunity of privileged
SamitiCommunity of common people
VidhataCommunity for religious purpose

Women could participate in both Sabha and Samiti

Ranking of Officials

OfficialRole
PurohitPriest
SenaniArmy Chief
GramaniVillage head

Religion

  • They worshiped nature (naturalistic polytheism) and no animals were worshipped.
  • They did not worship any idol.
  • They performed sacrificial prayers.

Inverted pyramid diagram: Rashtra (top) → Jana → Visa → Grama → Kula (bottom)

Deities

DeitiesGod Of
IndraPurandara; destroyer of forts (lord of plough)
Prithvi
AgniIntermediary between human and God
Soma
Vayu
RudraProtector of cattles
AditiMother of Indra
SavitriGayatri Mantra is dedicated to her

Pottery

  • Ochre/black and red ware coloured pottery was used.

Later Vedic Period (1000-600 BC)

  • Other three vedas were compiled.

Ganga Yamuna Doab

  • Aryans expanded from Punjab to western Uttar Pradesh.
  • Upper portion: Kuru
  • Middle part: Panchal
  • Iron was used for the first time.
  • → Towards the later vedic period, they shift from Doab area to eastern Up.
  • Expansion was possible due to: Iron weapons + Horses
  • Krishna Ayas/Shyam Ayas (black metal)
  • Ayas means: Metals

Agriculture

  • It was a chief means of livelihood.
  • King also did manual labour in the field.
  • Vrihi means rice. Godhuma: Wheat
  • Yava means barley. Dhanya: Grains and Cereals

Political Organisation

  • The political organisation became centralised.
BodyStatus
SabhaDominated by Brahmins; women participation not allowed now
SamitiSame as before (early Vedic period)
VidhataDisappeared during later Vedic period

Society: Varna System

VarnaRole
BrahmansPerformed rituals/sacrifices
KshatriyaParticipated in war and protected people
VaishyaConducts trade
SudraThey did manual work
  • Conditions of women deteriorated.
  • Gotra (clan) system emerged.

Ashrams Mentioned in Jabala Upanishad

AshramPhase
Brahmacharya1st phase of life (0-25 yrs)
Grihasta2nd phase of life (25-50)
Vanaprastha3rd phase of life
Sannyasa4th phase of life

Marriage

  • Anulom vivah: Boy is from higher caste + girl is from lower caste.
  • Pratiloma vivah: Girl is from higher caste + boy is from lower caste.

Eight types of marriage are there:

TypeDescription
Brahma VivahMarriage within same Varna with Vedic rituals
Gandharva VivahLove marriage
Daiva VivahFather donates his daughter to priest as Dakshina
Arsha VivahToken bride price of a cow and Bull were given
Prajapati VivahMarriage without dowry
Asur VivahMarriage by purchase

§ 5VEDIC AGE

Marriage (continued)

TypeDescription
Rakshasa VivahMarriage by abduction
Paishacha VivahIn this type of marriage, a girl who is not in her senses is forcibly married off

Religion

  • Other Gods like Rudra gained more importance while Indra and Agni lost their importance.
  • Pushan (god of cattle) came to be regarded as God of Shudras.
  • Prajapati: Creator of Universe
  • Idol worship gained importance.
  • Animal sacrifice increased during this period.
  • Different kind of Yajnas were performed. Ashwamedha yajna, Rajasuya sacrifice, vajapya.

Pottery

  • Grey coloured pottery were seen here.

Early vs Later Vedic Period

Early Vedic PeriodLater Vedic Period
Pastoral communityAgriculturists
Better women conditionCondition of women deteriorated
Varna system was based on profession and was not rigidVarna system became hereditary and rigid
No idol worshipIdol worship started
Rigveda was compiled during this timeSamveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda were compiled during this time
